services.title: Railway Machine Tool Services & Support
services.description: Installation, maintenance contracts, spare parts, retro-fitment, repair, relocation, wet leasing and training for HYT wheel lathes and workshop machines.
services.h1: Services that keep railway machine tools productive for life
services.lede: A wheel lathe earns its value over decades, not on the day it is handed over. HYT installs, maintains, repairs, upgrades and can even operate its machines, so your workshop keeps re-profiling wheels whenever the fleet needs it.
services.summary: Installation, maintenance contracts, spares, upgrades, repair, relocation, wet leasing and training for HYT machines.

blocks.heading: When the wheel lathe stops, trains wait
paragraphs: A wheel lathe sits on the critical path of fleet availability. If it is out of action, wheelsets with flats or thin flanges cannot be restored, vehicles are held back from traffic and the workshop falls behind its maintenance plan. The cost of a lost day is measured in trains, not in machine hours.

We design and build our machines in-house, so our service engineers know them from the foundation bolts to the CNC program. That knowledge shortens diagnosis, keeps repairs right first time and lets us recommend the spares and upgrades that genuinely extend machine life.
Every service below can be taken on its own or combined into a long-term contract. Tell us how your workshop runs and we will propose the level of support that fits – no more, no less.
bullets: Support from the engineers who designed and built the machine
Clear contract scopes, so you always know what is covered
Genuine spare parts identified against your machine's build records

installation-commissioning.title: Installation & Commissioning of Wheel Lathes
installation-commissioning.description: Foundation drawings, installation supervision, alignment, trials on your own wheelsets and documented handover for HYT wheel lathes and workshop machines.
installation-commissioning.h1: Installation and commissioning of railway machine tools
installation-commissioning.lede: A machine's accuracy is set on the day it is installed. Our engineers take it from foundation to proven production on your own wheelsets, and hand it over with full documentation.
installation-commissioning.summary: From foundation drawings to acceptance trials on your wheelsets – installed and commissioned by the engineers who built the machine.

blocks.heading: Accuracy starts with the foundation
paragraphs: An underfloor wheel lathe is part of the building: it sits in a pit beneath the track and must line up with the rails above it. A portal or surface lathe needs a level, stable foundation that will not settle under heavy wheelsets. Small errors at this stage show up for years afterwards as profile deviations, vibration and premature wear.

That is why HYT treats installation as engineering work, not as a delivery task. We issue foundation and pit drawings early in the project, check the site before the machine is shipped, and send engineers who know the machine's design to erect, align and prove it.
The result is a machine that meets its acceptance criteria on your own vehicles and wheelsets, and a team that knows how to run it from the first shift.
blocks.image_alt: Sample illustration of engineers aligning a wheel lathe module during installation in a workshop

items.title: Receipt and placement

items.title: Connections

items.title: Trials
items.text: Dry runs are followed by machining on your own wheelsets, with results measured against the agreed profile tolerances.

items.title: Training and handover
items.text: Operators and maintainers are trained, documents are handed over and the acceptance protocol is signed jointly.

blocks.heading: Installing without stopping the workshop
paragraphs: Many installations take place in depots that must keep running. Building a pit under an operational road, diverting cables or bringing heavy assemblies through a busy shed all need careful planning with your traffic and safety teams.

We agree work windows, isolation procedures and lifting plans in advance, and keep the footprint of our activities as small as possible. Where a complete facility is involved, our [Turnkey (EPC) Projects](page:turnkey-project) team can take responsibility for civil works and interfaces as well. Moving an existing machine to a new location is covered by our [SPM relocation and shifting](page:shifting) service.
blocks.image_alt: Sample illustration of a reinforced concrete pit being prepared beneath a depot track for a wheel lathe

items.q: How early should we involve HYT?
items.a: As soon as the machine is ordered – ideally while the depot layout is still being finalised. Pit and foundation drawings influence civil design and schedule, so early agreement saves time later.

items.q: Who carries out the civil works?
items.a: Normally your civil contractor, working to HYT drawings. We check the interface points before the machine arrives. In a turnkey project, civil works can be included in HYT's scope.

items.q: How long does commissioning take?
items.a: It depends on the machine type, site readiness and the availability of trial wheelsets. We share a realistic schedule with the offer and update it after the site readiness check.

items.q: Is operator training part of commissioning?
items.a: Yes. Initial training for operators and maintenance staff is delivered during commissioning. Extended or refresher programmes are available through our [Training](page:training) service.

items.q: What happens after handover?
items.a: Your machine enters its warranty period. Many customers then continue with an [Annual Maintenance Contract](page:annual-maintenance-contract) or a [Comprehensive Maintenance Contract](page:comprehensive-annual-maintenance-contract).

blocks.heading: Planning a new machine installation?
blocks.text: Send us your depot layout and the machine you are considering. We will tell you what the site needs and when.

maintenance.title: Maintenance Services & Contracts for Wheel Lathes
maintenance.description: Compare HYT maintenance contracts – O&M, AMC, CMC, operation, call-based service and spares support – and choose the right cover for your wheel lathe.
maintenance.lede: Six ways to keep your HYT machine available, from a call-based service agreement to full operation and maintenance by our own team. Compare the scopes and choose what fits your depot.
maintenance.summary: Compare O&M, AMC, CMC, operation, service and spares contracts and choose the right level of cover.

blocks.heading: Planned maintenance costs less than downtime
paragraphs: A wheel lathe works hard: heavy wheelsets, hard and worn treads, abrasive chips and long shifts. Guideways, rollers, hydraulics and measuring systems all need regular attention. Left alone, small faults become breakdowns – usually at the moment the fleet needs the machine most.

Our maintenance contracts put that attention on a schedule. They differ in three ways: who operates the machine, whether spare parts are included, and how the work is paid for. Choose the combination that matches your in-house skills, your budget model and how critical the machine is to fleet availability.
blocks.image_alt: Sample illustration of a technician inspecting the hydraulic unit of a wheel lathe during a preventive maintenance visit

blocks.heading: Contract types compared
blocks.intro: A typical scope for each contract type. Every contract is tailored, so the final inclusions and exclusions are set out in the offer.
rows: Depots without their own lathe team
Own operators, fixed budget including spares
Own maintenance team, no trained operators
blocks.note: Damage from accidents, misuse, power supply faults or civil defects, and upgrades or retro-fitment, are outside the standard scope of all contracts unless agreed.

blocks.heading: Which contract is right for us?

items.q: We have operators but no specialist maintenance staff.
items.a: An [AMC](page:annual-maintenance-contract) gives you scheduled preventive visits and breakdown attendance. If you also want spare parts covered within a fixed annual budget, choose a [CMC](page:comprehensive-annual-maintenance-contract).

items.q: We are opening a new depot and have no trained lathe team.
items.a: An [O&M contract](page:operation-and-maintenance) lets HYT operate and maintain the machine. If your maintenance department will look after the machine, an [Operation Contract](page:operation-contract) covers the operators only.

items.q: Our machine is lightly used and our own team maintains it.
items.a: A call-based [Service Contract](page:service-contract) gives you agreed rates for visits when you need them, and [Spare Parts & Support](page:spare-supply) keeps genuine parts within reach.

items.q: Can contracts be combined or changed later?
items.a: Yes. Many customers start with an O&M contract while training their own staff, then move to a CMC or AMC. We review the scope with you at each renewal.

blocks.heading: Not sure which contract fits?
blocks.text: Tell us about your machine, its utilisation and your in-house team. We will recommend a contract and send a clear scope of work.

operation-and-maintenance.title: Operation & Maintenance (O&M) Contracts
operation-and-maintenance.description: With an HYT O&M contract, our operators run your wheel lathe and our technicians maintain it – planned maintenance, breakdown cover and reporting included.
operation-and-maintenance.h1: Operation & Maintenance (O&M) contracts for wheel lathes
operation-and-maintenance.lede: HYT operators run the machine and HYT technicians maintain it. You receive re-profiled wheelsets on schedule without having to build a specialist lathe team of your own.
operation-and-maintenance.summary: HYT operators run your machine and HYT technicians maintain it – one contract, one point of accountability.

blocks.heading: One team responsible for output and machine health
paragraphs: Running a CNC wheel lathe well takes more than pressing start. Operators must position vehicles safely, interpret measurement results, choose the right profile and recognise early signs of trouble. Maintaining the machine requires mechanical, hydraulic, electrical and CNC skills that many depots do not have in-house.

Under an O&M contract, HYT provides both. Our operators work to your shift pattern and maintenance plan; our technicians keep the machine in condition with planned maintenance and attend breakdowns. Because the same organisation is responsible for operation and maintenance, there is no argument about whether a stoppage was caused by the operator or by the machine.
O&M suits new depots that have not yet trained a lathe team, operators that outsource specialist activities by policy, and high-utilisation machines where every hour of availability counts.
blocks.image_alt: Sample illustration of a metro depot with a train positioned over an underfloor wheel lathe

items.q: How is O&M different from an Operation Contract?
items.a: An O&M contract covers both operation and maintenance. An [Operation Contract](page:operation-contract) provides operators only; maintenance stays with your team or a separate [AMC](page:annual-maintenance-contract) or [CMC](page:comprehensive-annual-maintenance-contract).

items.q: Do our own staff need to be present?
items.a: Your depot remains in charge of rolling stock movements, safety permits and the maintenance plan. A nominated supervisor on your side keeps coordination simple.

items.q: Can our staff be trained to take over later?
items.a: Yes. An O&M contract can include structured [training](page:training) so that your team gradually takes over operation, with HYT continuing under an AMC or CMC.

items.q: How is the contract priced?
items.a: Usually as a periodic fee based on shifts, workload and the agreed scope. We quote after understanding your fleet and depot routine.

annual-maintenance-contract.title: Annual Maintenance Contract (AMC) for Machines
annual-maintenance-contract.description: An HYT Annual Maintenance Contract covers scheduled preventive visits and breakdown attendance by trained engineers. Spare parts are quoted separately.
annual-maintenance-contract.lede: Planned preventive visits and breakdown attendance from engineers who know your machine, for a fixed annual fee. Your team operates the machine; we keep it in good health.
annual-maintenance-contract.summary: Scheduled preventive visits and breakdown attendance for a fixed annual fee; spare parts quoted separately.

blocks.heading: Predictable labour cost, planned machine care
paragraphs: An AMC is the most common way to keep an HYT machine in condition after the warranty period. Your operators continue to run the machine every day. HYT engineers visit at agreed intervals to inspect, adjust and service it, and attend when something goes wrong.

The fee covers our engineers' time for the agreed number of preventive visits and for breakdown attendance during the contract year. Spare parts are not included: when a part is needed, we tell you which one, why and what it costs, and supply it against your order. If you would rather have spares within a fixed budget too, look at the [Comprehensive Maintenance Contract (CMC)](page:comprehensive-annual-maintenance-contract).
Regular visits catch wear before it causes a breakdown, keep machining accuracy within limits and build a service history that helps when planning upgrades or replacement.

items.q: What is the difference between an AMC and a CMC?
items.a: An AMC covers labour for preventive visits and breakdown attendance. A [CMC](page:comprehensive-annual-maintenance-contract) adds the spare parts listed in the contract, so your annual maintenance cost is fixed.

items.q: How many preventive visits are included?
items.a: The number is agreed with you, based on machine type, utilisation and operating conditions. It is stated in the contract.

items.q: Can we take an AMC for an older machine?
items.a: Yes, after a condition inspection. If the machine needs repairs first, we will quote those separately – see [Repair](page:repair).

items.q: What response time can we expect for a breakdown?
items.a: Response commitments are written into each contract, based on the machine's location and how critical it is to your fleet. We agree them with you before the contract starts, so there is no ambiguity when a call comes in.

items.q: How do we report a breakdown?
items.a: Call the toll-free service line 1800 2100 456 or email us with the machine serial number and a description of the fault. See [After-Sales Service Network](page:service-centers).

comprehensive-annual-maintenance-contrac.title: Comprehensive Maintenance Contract (CMC)
comprehensive-annual-maintenance-contrac.description: HYT's Comprehensive Maintenance Contract adds spare parts to preventive visits and breakdown attendance, giving you a predictable annual maintenance cost.
comprehensive-annual-maintenance-contrac.lede: Preventive maintenance, breakdown attendance and the spare parts to fix the machine – all within one annual fee. A CMC turns maintenance from an unpredictable cost into a fixed budget line.
comprehensive-annual-maintenance-contrac.summary: Preventive visits, breakdown attendance and listed spare parts within one fixed annual fee.

blocks.heading: Maintenance and spares under one fixed fee
paragraphs: A CMC includes everything in an [Annual Maintenance Contract](page:annual-maintenance-contract) – scheduled preventive visits and breakdown attendance – and adds the spare parts needed to keep the machine running. When a covered part fails or reaches the end of its life, HYT supplies and fits it without a separate purchase order.

That matters in organisations where procurement of a single part can take longer than the repair itself. With a CMC, the machine is back in service as soon as the part arrives, and your annual maintenance cost is known in advance.

Because HYT carries the cost of parts, we have every reason to maintain the machine thoroughly and to replace wear parts before they cause damage elsewhere. Your operators continue to run the machine; we take care of its condition.

operation-contract.description: Under an HYT Operation Contract, trained HYT operators run your wheel lathe while maintenance stays with your own team or a separate maintenance contract.

operation-contract.lede: HYT operators run the machine; maintenance remains with your own team or under a separate contract. You gain skilled operation without handing over machine upkeep.

blocks.text: This service overlaps with Operation & Maintenance (O&M). HYT to confirm that both pages should remain and that the scope below (operation only, maintenance excluded) is correct.

blocks.heading: Operation only – a clear, narrow scope
paragraphs: Some depots have a strong maintenance department but no operators trained on a CNC wheel lathe. Others face a temporary gap: a new machine arriving before staff are recruited, or a period of high re-profiling demand. An Operation Contract fills that gap with HYT operators who know the machine, its measuring system and its profile programs.

Our operators work to your shift pattern and maintenance plan. They position wheelsets, measure, select the correct profile, machine and record the result. They carry out operator-level care – cleaning, routine lubrication and daily checks – and report any abnormality to your maintenance team straight away.

Preventive maintenance, breakdown repair and spare parts are not part of this contract. They remain with your own team or can be placed with HYT under an [AMC](page:annual-maintenance-contract) or [CMC](page:comprehensive-annual-maintenance-contract). If you prefer one contract for everything, choose [Operation & Maintenance (O&M)](page:operation-and-maintenance).

blocks.heading: Flexible support without an annual commitment
paragraphs: Not every machine needs a full maintenance contract. A lathe that runs a few shifts a month, or a workshop with an experienced in-house maintenance team, may only need specialist help occasionally. A Service Contract sets the commercial terms in advance so that, when you do need us, nothing is held up by negotiation or purchase approvals.

We agree a rate card with you – engineer day rates, travel and any standard charges – for an agreed period. When you raise a call, we assign an engineer, attend, diagnose and repair, and invoice for that visit only. Preventive visits can be booked on the same terms whenever you choose.

If your call volume grows, an [Annual Maintenance Contract](page:annual-maintenance-contract) or [CMC](page:comprehensive-annual-maintenance-contract) will usually work out more economical and gives you scheduled preventive care. We will tell you when that point is reached.

items.a: Yes. If your call volume grows or you want scheduled preventive care, we can convert the agreement to an [AMC](page:annual-maintenance-contract) or [CMC](page:comprehensive-annual-maintenance-contract) at any time.

items.q: Are spare parts available under a Service Contract?
items.a: Yes, quoted separately for each requirement. See [Spare Parts & Support](page:spare-supply).

blocks.heading: Set up a Service Contract
blocks.text: Send us your machine details and we will propose a rate card and contract period.

spare-supply.title: Spare Parts & Technical Support for Wheel Lathes
spare-supply.description: Genuine spare parts, recommended spares lists, obsolescence planning and telephone technical support for HYT wheel lathes and wheel shop machines.
spare-supply.lede: Genuine parts matched to your machine's build records, and engineers on the phone who can help your team fit them correctly. Fewer delays, fewer wrong parts, longer machine life.
spare-supply.summary: Genuine spare parts, recommended spares lists and technical support for HYT machines.

blocks.heading: The right part, first time
paragraphs: Machines built over several decades and configured for different gauges, profiles and vehicle types are rarely identical. The roller, seal or sensor that fits one machine may not fit the next. We identify spares against your machine's serial number and build records, so the part that arrives is the part that fits.
Genuine parts are made to the original drawings and materials. That protects machining accuracy, avoids damage to mating components and keeps your warranty and contract terms intact.
For workshops that maintain their machines themselves, our engineers are available by phone and email to advise on fault-finding, part replacement and settings.
blocks.image_alt: Sample illustration of labelled spare parts for wheel lathes on shelves in a parts store

blocks.heading: Spares and support for the whole machine

items.title: Mechanical parts
items.text: Rollers, bearings, slides, ball screws, clamping elements and other wear parts.

items.title: Hydraulic and pneumatic
items.text: Valves, cylinders, pumps, seals and fittings for the machine's fluid systems.

items.title: Electrical and CNC
items.text: Drives, motors, sensors, control components and cabinet parts.

items.title: Measuring system parts
items.text: Probes and components for the wheel profile measuring system.

items.title: Recommended spares lists
items.text: Lists of critical and wear parts to hold on site, ranked by risk and lead time.

items.title: Obsolescence planning
items.text: Early notice when components are being discontinued, with alternatives or upgrade paths.

items.title: Identify

items.title: Confirm
items.text: We check the part against your machine's records and confirm the correct item.

items.title: Quote

items.title: Dispatch

items.title: Support

blocks.heading: Hold the parts that stop the machine
paragraphs: Some parts wear predictably; others fail rarely but stop the machine when they do. Holding a small stock of the critical items on site can turn a week of downtime into a few hours. Our recommended spares list ranks parts by how critical they are to operation and how long they take to source, so you can decide what to keep in your store and what to order when needed.
We review the list with you as the machine ages, when components are discontinued, and after a [retro-fitment](page:retro-fitment-upgradation) changes the machine's configuration.

items: Machine model and serial number

Photographs of the part and its nameplate, if any
Quantity required

items.q: Can you supply parts for older machines?
items.a: Yes, wherever possible. If an original component is no longer made, we propose an equivalent or a [retro-fitment](page:retro-fitment-upgradation) of the affected system.

items.q: Which spares should we hold on site?
items.a: Ask for the recommended spares list for your machine. It ranks parts by how critical they are and how long they take to source.

items.q: Are spare parts included in maintenance contracts?
items.a: They are included in a [CMC](page:comprehensive-annual-maintenance-contract), as listed in the contract. Under an [AMC](page:annual-maintenance-contract), parts are quoted separately.

items.q: How quickly can a part be delivered?
items.a: It depends on the part. Some items are held in stock; others are manufactured or sourced to order. The quotation states the delivery time, and if your machine is stopped, tell us so that we can prioritise.

items.q: Can you fit the parts for us?
items.a: Yes. Our engineers can attend on site under a [Service Contract](page:service-contract) or as a one-off visit.

blocks.heading: Need a spare part?
blocks.text: Send the machine serial number and the part details. If your machine is stopped, call the toll-free line 1800 2100 456.

retro-fitment-upgradation.title: Retro-fitment & Upgradation of Wheel Lathes
retro-fitment-upgradation.description: Extend the life of your wheel lathe: new CNC systems, drives, measuring technology and safety upgrades fitted to a sound machine structure by HYT engineers.
retro-fitment-upgradation.h1: Retro-fitment and upgradation of wheel lathes
retro-fitment-upgradation.lede: A well-built machine structure can outlast its control system by decades. Retro-fitment replaces what is obsolete and keeps what is sound, giving you a modern machine for a fraction of the disruption of a new one.
retro-fitment-upgradation.summary: New CNC systems, drives, measuring technology and safety upgrades for machines with a sound structure.

blocks.heading: Keep the structure, renew the intelligence
paragraphs: Machine beds, frames and slideways are built to last. Control systems, drives and electronics are not: within a decade or two, components are discontinued, spares become hard to source and every breakdown takes longer to fix. At the same time, newer controls offer better diagnostics, easier programming and profile measurement that saves wheel material.

Retro-fitment addresses both problems. We assess the machine, keep the parts that are still sound and replace the systems that limit availability or performance. For an underfloor lathe, it also avoids the civil works and long shutdown that a new pit machine would require.
Our first concern is HYT machines, whose designs we know in detail. If your machine is from another manufacturer, send us the details and we will tell you honestly whether an assessment makes sense.
blocks.image_alt: Sample illustration of a modern CNC operator panel showing a wheel profile on screen

items.title: CNC system
items.text: A current industrial CNC with railway-specific cycles, profile libraries and on-screen diagnostics.

items.title: Drives and motors
items.text: New servo and main drives for reliable performance and available spares.

items.title: Measuring system
items.text: Automatic wheel profile measurement so only the necessary material is removed.

items.title: Hydraulics
items.text: Overhauled or replaced power packs, valves and cylinders.

items.title: Safety
items.text: Updated guarding, interlocks and emergency-stop circuits to current practice.

items.title: Data and reporting
items.text: Machining reports and measurement records that can be exported for fleet maintenance systems.

blocks.heading: Signs that a machine is ready for retro-fitment
items: Control or drive spares are discontinued or hard to source
Breakdowns take longer to diagnose because diagnostics are limited
The machine cannot store or measure the profiles your fleet now needs
Measurement data has to be recorded by hand
Guarding or interlocks no longer meet your safety standards
The structure and geometry are still sound

items.title: Condition assessment
items.text: Our engineers inspect the structure, geometry, hydraulics and electrics and review the machine's history.

items.title: Proposal
items.text: We recommend a scope – from a single system to a full rebuild – with the benefits and risks of each option.

items.title: Engineering
items.text: New electrical, hydraulic and software designs are prepared and components procured before the shutdown.

items.title: Shutdown and execution
items.text: The machine is taken out of service only when parts are ready, keeping downtime as short as possible.

items.title: Re-commissioning
items.text: Geometry, measuring and machining are proven on your wheelsets against agreed criteria.

items.title: Training and handover
items.text: Operators and maintainers are trained on the new systems and documentation is updated.

items.q: Retrofit or new machine – how do we decide?
items.a: If the structure and geometry are sound, a retrofit usually costs less and avoids civil works. If the structure is worn or your requirements have changed significantly, a new machine may be better. Our assessment sets out both options.

items.q: How long will the machine be out of service?
items.a: That depends on the scope. We plan engineering and procurement before the shutdown so that the machine is down only for installation and re-commissioning.

items.q: Will our operators need retraining?
items.a: Yes, on the new control and any new functions. [Training](page:training) is part of every retro-fitment project.

items.q: Can a retrofit add new wheel profiles?
items.a: Yes. New profiles for changed fleets can be added to the CNC as part of the upgrade.

blocks.heading: Is your machine due for an upgrade?
blocks.text: Send us the model, serial number and the problems you are seeing. We will propose a condition assessment.

repair.title: Wheel Lathe & Machine Tool Repair Services
repair.description: Breakdown and major repairs for HYT wheel lathes and wheel shop machines: fault-finding, mechanical rebuilds, hydraulic and electrical repair, tested on site.
repair.h1: Repair of wheel lathes and wheel shop machines
repair.lede: From a sudden breakdown to a planned rebuild after years of heavy use, our engineers find the cause, fix it properly and prove the machine before returning it to your team.
repair.summary: Breakdown and major repairs: diagnosis, mechanical, hydraulic and electrical work, tested before handover.

blocks.heading: Fix the cause, not just the symptom
paragraphs: A repair that only restores the machine for a week costs more than one done properly the first time. Our engineers look for the root cause – a worn guide, a contaminated hydraulic circuit, a failing sensor – before replacing parts, and they tell you what they found and why it happened.
Because we designed the machine, we have its drawings, settings and parts records. That shortens diagnosis and means repairs restore the original accuracy, not an approximation of it.

Repairs are available to every HYT customer, with or without a maintenance contract. Customers with an [AMC](page:annual-maintenance-contract) or [CMC](page:comprehensive-annual-maintenance-contract) have breakdown attendance included in their contract.
blocks.image_alt: Sample illustration of engineers dismantling a wheel lathe assembly for repair

items.title: Breakdown repair
items.text: Fault-finding and rectification to get a stopped machine back into service.

items.title: Mechanical rebuilds
items.text: Slides, guideways, ball screws, rollers and clamping systems reconditioned or replaced.

items.title: Hydraulic repair
items.text: Leak rectification, cylinder and valve overhaul and circuit flushing.

blocks.intro: The more we know before an engineer travels, the more likely the first visit fixes the problem.

items.q: Do you repair machines from other manufacturers?
items.a: Our expertise is in HYT machines, whose designs and records we hold. For other makes, send us the details and we will tell you honestly whether we can help.

items.q: Do we need a maintenance contract to get a repair?
items.a: No. Repairs are available to all HYT customers. A [Service Contract](page:service-contract) fixes the rates in advance and speeds up approvals.

items.q: Can repairs be done on site?
items.a: Most repairs are carried out on site. Where an assembly needs machining or a full rebuild, it may be brought to our works in Pune.

items.q: What if the original parts are no longer available?
items.a: We propose an equivalent part or a targeted [retro-fitment](page:retro-fitment-upgradation) of the affected system.

blocks.heading: Machine down?
blocks.text: Call 1800 2100 456 with the machine serial number, or send us the details and we will respond as quickly as possible.

shifting.title: SPM Relocation & Shifting Services
shifting.description: Planned relocation of special purpose machines (SPMs) such as wheel lathes: survey, dismantling, transport, foundation preparation and re-commissioning.
shifting.lede: Moving a wheel lathe or other special purpose machine (SPM) is a project, not a lift. We dismantle, move, re-install and re-commission it so that it performs at the new site as it did at the old one.
shifting.summary: Survey, dismantling, transport, re-installation and re-commissioning of wheel lathes and other SPMs.

blocks.heading: Precision machines do not travel well on their own
paragraphs: Depots are rebuilt, fleets move to new sheds and workshops are reorganised. When that happens, a special purpose machine such as a wheel lathe, wheel press or vertical turning machine often moves with them. These machines are heavy, precisely aligned and, in the case of underfloor lathes, built into the track.

A poorly planned move risks damaged assemblies, lost alignment and a long, uncertain re-commissioning. HYT plans each relocation from start to finish: we record the machine's condition and accuracy before dismantling, prepare the new foundation drawings, and re-commission the machine to the same acceptance criteria at its new home.
Relocation is also a good moment to fit upgrades. Many customers combine a move with a [retro-fitment](page:retro-fitment-upgradation) of the control system or an overhaul of worn assemblies.
blocks.image_alt: Sample illustration of a wheel lathe assembly being lifted by crane during relocation

items.title: Survey
items.text: Inspection of the machine and both sites, with a record of condition and accuracy before the move.

items.title: New site preparation
items.text: Foundation or pit drawings issued for the new location, and readiness checked before dismantling begins.

items.title: Dismantling
items.text: Assemblies are separated, marked and documented in a planned sequence.

items.title: Packing and transport
items.text: Precision surfaces are protected and assemblies are packed and secured for the route.

items.title: Re-installation
items.text: The machine is placed, levelled, aligned and reconnected at the new site.

items.title: Re-commissioning
items.text: Trials on your wheelsets prove that the machine meets its acceptance criteria.

items.title: Documented baseline
items.text: Before-and-after accuracy records prove the machine performs as it did.

items.title: Planned downtime
items.text: A clear schedule agreed with you so that workshop capacity can be planned around the move.

items.title: Upgrade opportunity
items.text: Combine the move with an overhaul or retro-fitment while the machine is out of service.

items.q: What is an SPM?
items.a: A special purpose machine – a machine tool designed for a specific task, such as re-profiling railway wheels, pressing wheels on to axles or turning axle journals.

items.q: Can you relocate an underfloor wheel lathe?
items.a: Yes. Underfloor lathes need a new pit at the destination, so civil works must be planned early. We supply the pit drawings and check the pit before the machine is moved.

items.q: How long will the machine be out of service?
items.a: It depends on the machine, the distance and how ready the new site is. Preparing the new foundation or pit before dismantling begins is the most effective way to shorten the move, and we plan the schedule around it.

items.q: Who arranges transport?
items.a: This is agreed per project. HYT can plan and manage the full move, or work with your nominated logistics contractor.

items.q: Will the warranty or maintenance contract continue?
items.a: Contract terms are reviewed as part of the relocation. After successful re-commissioning, an [AMC](page:annual-maintenance-contract) or [CMC](page:comprehensive-annual-maintenance-contract) can continue at the new site.

blocks.heading: Planning a move?
blocks.text: Tell us which machine is moving, from where and to where. We will propose a survey and a relocation plan.

wet-leasing.nav: MAAS – Machine as a Service (Wet Leasing)
wet-leasing.title: Machine as a Service (Wet Leasing) for Wheel Lathes
wet-leasing.description: Machine as a Service: HYT supplies the wheel lathe, operators and maintenance under one agreement, so you pay for re-profiling capacity instead of capital.
wet-leasing.h1: Machine as a Service (MAAS): wet leasing of wheel lathes
wet-leasing.lede: HYT provides the machine, the people who run it and the maintenance that keeps it running. You receive re-profiled wheelsets without the capital investment or the need to build a specialist team.
wet-leasing.summary: We supply the machine, operators and maintenance; you pay for re-profiling capacity rather than capital equipment.

blocks.heading: Pay for re-profiled wheels, not for a machine
paragraphs: Buying a wheel lathe means capital approval, a procurement process, civil works, recruitment and training – before a single wheel is machined. For some operators that is the right path. For others, especially those facing an urgent capacity gap or uncertain long-term demand, it is not.

With Machine as a Service, HYT supplies a wheel lathe together with trained operators and full maintenance under one agreement. The term "wet leasing" comes from aviation, where an aircraft is leased with its crew. Here, the machine comes with its crew too.

You define the output you need. We keep the machine productive and are responsible for its availability. The commercial model – a periodic fee, a rate per wheelset or a combination – is agreed for each project.

items.title: The machine
items.text: A suitable HYT wheel lathe, installed and commissioned at your site.

items.title: The crew
items.text: Trained HYT operators working to your shift pattern.

items.title: Maintenance
items.text: Preventive maintenance, breakdown attendance and spares management by HYT.

items.title: Reporting
items.text: Records of wheelsets machined and measurement results for your fleet systems.

blocks.heading: Buy, O&M or Machine as a Service?
rows: Owned asset without an in-house lathe team
Fast capacity, limited capital or temporary demand
blocks.note: Civil works for the pit or foundation and the commercial model are agreed for each project.

blocks.heading: When Machine as a Service makes sense
items: A new depot needs re-profiling capacity before a machine can be procured
Capital budgets are constrained but operating budgets are available
Demand is temporary – a fleet introduction, a backlog or a major overhaul campaign
The organisation prefers to outsource specialist maintenance activities
A trial period is needed before deciding on a permanent machine
In-house staff are not yet trained on CNC wheel lathes

items.text: Fleet, workload, site and duration are reviewed with you.

items.title: Proposal
items.text: We recommend a machine, a team and a commercial model.

items.text: Pit or foundation works are agreed and completed to HYT drawings.

items.title: Installation
items.text: The machine is installed and commissioned on your wheelsets.

items.text: HYT operates and maintains the machine and reports output regularly.

items.text: Extend the agreement, transfer to an [O&M](page:operation-and-maintenance) model or plan a permanent machine.

items.q: How is wet leasing different from O&M?
items.a: Under an [O&M contract](page:operation-and-maintenance), you own the machine and HYT runs and maintains it. With Machine as a Service, HYT also provides the machine.

items.q: Who prepares the pit or foundation?
items.a: This is agreed per project. HYT supplies the drawings and checks the works; the civil construction is usually arranged by the customer.

items.q: Which machines are available?
items.a: The machine is selected for your fleet and site, typically an [underfloor wheel lathe](page:underfloor-wheel-lathe). Talk to us about your requirement.

blocks.heading: Need capacity without capital?
blocks.text: Tell us about your fleet, your depot and how long you need the capacity. We will propose a Machine as a Service model.

training.title: Training for Wheel Lathe Operators & Maintainers
training.description: Hands-on training for operators, CNC programmers and maintenance teams on HYT wheel lathes and wheel shop machines – on site, at our works or as refreshers.
training.h1: Training for operators, programmers and maintainers
training.lede: A machine is only as good as the people who run it. Our training gives your team the skill and confidence to machine accurately, work safely and keep the machine in condition.
training.summary: Hands-on training for operators, programmers and maintenance teams – on site, at our works or as refreshers.

blocks.heading: Skilled operators save wheel material
paragraphs: Every millimetre removed from a wheel tread shortens the wheel's life. An operator who understands the measuring system, chooses the right profile and recognises when a cut can be reduced protects wheel life and reduces cost per kilometre. An operator who does not can turn a precise machine into an expensive one.
The same applies to maintenance. Teams that know what to check, what normal looks like and how to read the machine's diagnostics catch problems before they become breakdowns.
Our trainers are engineers who build, commission and service HYT machines. Training uses your own machine wherever possible, so your team learns on the equipment they will use every day.
blocks.image_alt: Sample illustration of an HYT trainer explaining a wheel lathe control panel to depot staff

items.text: Safe positioning, measuring, profile selection, machining cycles and daily care.

items.title: CNC programmers
items.text: Profile programs, parameters, machining strategies and measurement data.

items.title: Mechanical maintainers

blocks.heading: Typical training topics
blocks.intro: Content is tailored to your machine and your team's experience. A typical programme covers:
items: Machine layout, safety zones, guards and emergency procedures
Positioning vehicles or wheelsets and clamping correctly
Wheel profile measurement and interpreting the results
Selecting profiles and minimising material removal
Running machining cycles and checking the finished profile
Daily, weekly and periodic maintenance tasks
Hydraulic, pneumatic and lubrication systems
Reading alarms and using the CNC diagnostics
Replacing common wear parts and cutting inserts
Keeping machining and maintenance records

items: Initial training during installation and commissioning
On-site courses on your own machine
Sessions at the HYT works in Pune, on request
Refresher courses for experienced staff
Induction training for new team members
Training on new functions after a retro-fitment

items.title: Delivery

items.title: Assessment

items.q: Is training included with a new machine?
items.a: Yes. Initial training for operators and maintainers is part of [installation and commissioning](page:installation-commissioning).

items.a: Yes. We tailor the content to the machine's configuration and control system.

service-centers.lede: One number, one service desk and engineers who know your machine. Here is how to reach us and what happens after you call.

blocks.heading: Coordinated from Pune, delivered on site
paragraphs: Every service request is logged and coordinated by our service desk at the HYT works in Pune, where our machines are designed and built. The desk has access to each machine's build records, drawings and service history, so the first conversation is already an informed one.

Field service engineers travel to your site for installation, preventive maintenance, breakdowns and repairs. Where a machine supports remote connection, our engineers can review alarms and parameters before travelling, which often shortens diagnosis and ensures the right parts go with the engineer.
Spare parts are dispatched from Pune. For urgent cases, tell us that the machine is stopped and we will prioritise accordingly.
